claims.statement: For every finite ordinary connected tree T, with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T) the least natural index for which Delta_x(T)<0, x(T)+2<=p implies alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Exact auxiliary eligibility guard for finite ordinary connected trees, with strict first descent and integer p; no residuality premise and no aggregate conclusion.
claims.reason: The pinned r27 finite-forest lemma has the exact integer Delta and carrier hypotheses needed at k=x, yielding n<=4x. Eligibility and n>=alpha+1 reduce alpha<=6 to alpha=6, x=2, n=7 or 8. Exact pair/triple incidence formulas and maximum-independent-set complement covers force Delta_2>=5 or >=2, contradicting strict descent. Independent replay and a fresh larger eligible star check found no falsification; the proof is universal only through the stated bound, not the finite checks.

limitations: This is a proposed critique disposition of an auxiliary guard, not a new formal verification or an award of the primary aggregate.
The copied exhaustive calculation covers only labeled trees at orders 7 and 8; the universal conclusion relies on the pinned r27 descent lemma plus the cover argument.
The fresh K_{1,11} calculation checks one larger eligible tree and does not establish the tagged-shadow inequality or the complete aggregate generally.
